newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria postpones Devnya Cement sale signing.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria postpones Devnya Cement sale signing.

text.p: Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency on Monday postponed signing a deal for the sale of 70 percent of Devnya Cement to Bulgarian-Spanish consortium Marvex.

Rival French bidder Ciments Francais said last week Marvex's business plan lacked credibility and asked the Bulgarian government to investigate. The matter was raised in talks between Presidents Petar Stoyanov and Jacques Chirac in Paris.
The Privatisation Agency said the necessary bank guarantees had not been received by the central bank by Monday's deadline and it would propose that the deadline be put back by two or three days.
"We did not sign the contract due to a lack of a 100 percent guarantee," Privatisation Agency executive director Alexander Sabotinov told Reuters.
He said 10 percent of the $44.5 million purchase price had been transferred but the Agency required bank guarantees for the other 90 percent.

Ciments Francais said in a statement last week the lack of credibility of Marvex's offer was illustrated by the absence of financial details, the successive extensions of the negotiation period due to the consortium's inability to furnish bank guarantees, and the absence of a genuine business plan.

"At the moment Marvex is offering $4 million more. This is important for us, because $4 million is a significant figure," interim prime minister Stefan Sofianski told reporters before a cabinet meeting on Monday.
"The question is whether we have guarantees that we will receive these funds and whether we have guarantees that the (agreed) investment programme will be fulfilled," he said.
"If at some moment the commitments undertaken by Marvex are not fulfilled, I hope the next government, as I would have done, would break the deal and retain the money."
Sofianski is due to hand over this month to a new government following elections on April 19.
Ciments Francais is a unit of Italcementi Group.

The Marvex consortium was set up for the privatisation deal and the Spanish side, led by Moltiracion De Graneles, holds 80 percent. The remainder is held by Bulgarian private company ELVA, which distributes Russian Lada cars in Bulgaria.
Marvex has pledged to invest $209.5 million in the Devnya plant over the next five years.
Bulgaria's biggest sell-off to date, of a 60 percent stake in soda ash producer Sodi, was originally agreed with a U.S. buyer, General Chemical Group Inc.
That deal fell through after critics expressed concerns aboput the buyer, and the sale was finally completed with Belgium's Solvay.
